title: Private VPC Capacity Risk Register and Optimizer
content:
Purpose:
This working doc combines a compact risk register with a stochastic capacity optimizer for Private/VPC GPU fleets. The goal is not a final BOM but a decision-ready artefact that: 1) surfaces procurement and regional risks, 2) quantifies headroom needed (95th pct and P99) under mixed traffic, and 3) proposes a recommended GPU mix + spare strategy to minimize cost while keeping SLOs.

Scope and context:
- Target fleet: initial Private deployment for EU/NA with optional APAC edge pods.
- Workloads: interactive chat generation (latency-sensitive) and batch embeddings/reranking (throughput).
- Time horizon: purchase & delivery planning for next 12 months (Q1–Q4 2027).
- Baseline utilization target: 65% average, maintain <5% P99 latency SLO breaches for latency tier.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Average tokens per interactive request: 560 tokens
- Token mix: 60% generation, 40% embeddings/batch ops
- Model types: mix of Llama-3-70B quantized (fp16/8-bit) and an optimized 13B variant for low-latency tiers
- Instance candidates: A100-80GB, H100-80GB, and 8xA10-style dense racks for cheaper batch lanes
- Preemption risk for spot-like capacity: 15% monthly for vendor X in region EU-West3
- Lead times: 10–18 weeks for H100 series, 6–10 weeks for A100 procurement via preferred reseller
- Spare replacement lead time: 2 weeks (local spares) / 10 weeks (full replacement)

Monte Carlo optimizer (summary):
- Random variables: daily traffic growth (mu=0.8% ± sigma=1.2%), preemption events (Bernoulli p=0.15), supplier delay multiplier (lognormal, mean=1.0, sd=0.25).
- Output metrics per run: regional mGPU-hours required, expected P95 latency, spare pool depletion probability, 95th percentile cost/month.
- Runs: 10k trials. Key outputs attached as CSV in binder (see linked artifacts).

Representative scenario outputs (select highlights):
- P99 latency breach probability without spares (65% util target) under 20% unexpected traffic surge: 37%.
- Adding 8 H100s to NA central reduces P99 breach probability to 4.8% with 10k Monte Carlo runs (assumes intelligent routing fallback).
- Cheapest near-term solution (cost-weighted) to hit 95% uptime under preemption: mix of 60% reserved A100 + 40% preemptible H100 with 15% spare pool.

Risk register (condensed):
- R1 | Component shortages (vendor lead time spikes) | Likelihood: High | Impact: High | Mitigation: staggered orders across two resellers; maintain 10% spare pool; contract 60% as reserved capacity | Owner: Marta Ruiz
- R2 | Network egress throttles in APAC PoP | Likelihood: Medium | Impact: Medium | Mitigation: limit cross-region sharding for sensitive requests; enable partial fallbacks to NA; run synthetic egress tests weekly | Owner: Ethan Cho
- R3 | Model regression after quantization update causing throughput drop | Likelihood: Medium | Impact: High | Mitigation: A/B rollout with canary; reserve 2 racks for rollback; evaluation suite with perf+quality thresholds | Owner: Ayesha Kapoor
- R4 | Unexpected traffic pattern (token length spikes) | Likelihood: Medium | Impact: High | Mitigation: autoscale headroom lanes for short windows; adaptive KV cache rules to reduce redundant tokens | Owner: Priya Narayanan
- R5 | Regulatory hold-up for shipment (import compliance) in EU region | Likelihood: Low | Impact: Medium | Mitigation: pre-clear customs with reseller; maintain alternate vendor in EU | Owner: Liam O'Connor

Cost / BOM estimator (concise sample):
- Unit cost inputs used in optimizer (examples):
  - H100-80GB unit price (list): $45k; reseller negotiated: $37k; rack+network+power per unit incremental: $4k
  - A100-80GB unit price (list): $35k; negotiated: $30k; rack+network+power per unit incremental: $3.2k
  - Dense 8x A10 rack: $180k assembled (effective per-GPU: $22.5k incl power/pdu/cooling)
- Example calculation snippet: {units_needed} = ceil((expected_peak_mGPU_hours / (hours_per_month * per_gpu_hour_capacity_factor)))
- Sample BOM line (NA-central): 20 x A100-80GB (reserved) @ $30k + rack infra $64k => subtotal $664k.

Operational headroom & spare policy recommendation (concise):
- Maintain a dynamic spare pool sized to cover: max(5% of fleet, Nunits_to_cover_2w_replace), where Nunits_to_cover_2w_replace = units required to restore capacity if a 10% segment fails within 2 weeks.
- Regional allocation: NA 40% of spares, EU 50%, APAC 10% (APAC expensive to ship quickly).
- Spare rotation: swap spares into production monthly to verify hardware health; run burn-in workloads in lab prior to redeploy.

Procurement cadence & contracts:
- Stagger major purchases across Q1/Q2 to avoid single point of delivery failure.
- Negotiate partial-delivery SLAs and accelerate clauses for H100s (vendor rebates for >4 week delay).
- Build reseller A/B sourcing list and keep one C-tier emergency reseller for small incremental buys.

Capacity triggers & runbook (short):
- Traffic trigger: if rolling 6-hour avg utilization for latency lanes >78% for 3 consecutive days -> open capacity runbook.
- Preemption trigger: if preemptions >10% of expected in any week -> move 25% of low-latency traffic to reserved lanes and escalate procurement team.
- Runbook steps: 1) engage Sourcing (PR 1), 2) open emergency reserved pool in dedicated partner region, 3) enable cross-region routing to fallback model variant, 4) re-evaluate Monte Carlo outputs with latest telemetry.

Decision recommendations (current):
1) Approve an initial blended purchase: 48 A100 reserved (NA+EU split), 12 H100 reserved (EU priority), and a 16-GPU dense A10 rack for batch-only lanes.
2) Commit to a 10% spare pool physically distributed (per regional allocation above).
3) Run weekly Monte Carlo refreshes using live traffic feed and queue anomalies; publish scoreboard to Console -> capacity-dashboard route.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Confirm reseller negotiated price bands for H100 in EU (Marta to confirm by 2026-12-10).
- Validate per-request token distributions on production shadow traffic (Priya to run 2-week capture).
- Confirm tax/import timelines for APAC supplier once prospective partner responds (Liam).

Next steps and owners:

- Priya: deploy traffic capture and push to optimizer (due 2026-12-20).
- Ethan: setup synthetic egress throttles + weekly test job (due 2026-12-08).
- Ayesha: synchronize with product-hosted-api to align fallback model variants (due 2026-12-15).
